title: Understanding the Pattern
text:
The pattern .*:\w+(,\w+)+ is designed to match strings that have a colon followed by one or more words separated by commas. Let's break it down:

- .*: matches any character (except for a newline) zero or more times, followed by a colon.
- \w+ matches one or more word characters (letters, digits, or underscores).
- (,\w+)+ matches one or more occurrences of a comma followed by one or more word characters.

title: Checking the Pattern Against Each Case
text:
Let's check the pattern against each case:

$$1$$. "total cats petted: 60,102,305" - The pattern matches because it has a colon followed by numbers separated by commas.
$$2$$. "my cats' names are: amy,baron,carol" - The pattern matches because it has a colon followed by words separated by commas.
$$3$$. "the current time is 20:59" - The pattern does not match because it has a colon followed by a time format, not words separated by commas.
